The generic integral printf visitor delegates directly to detail::write, exactly as its original write(value) helper. It copies specs and changes numeric alignment to right only when integer precision is nonnegative. In the public vprintf path, integral precision>=0 resets fill to space before numeric alignment can be assigned, and numeric alignment is otherwise assigned only when fill is zero. The added conditional is consequently redundant for ordinary public printf precision calls; Char branch remains unchanged. Restores octal byte bound and replaces unchecked hex accumulation with generic sticky overflow: before the next digit, ch>15 means the resulting value cannot fit one byte. This prevents long values wrapping back into byte range, matching escaping.h documented arbitrary-length-one-byte contract. Both output conversions replace adding divisor-1 before unsigned division with rounding the fractional remainder up to a divisor multiple when nonzero. For bounded nonnegative x and divisor b, floor((x+b-1)/b) equals x/b plus (x%b!=0), exactly the new expression after division. Time nanosecond carry boundaries (4,000,000,000 ticks per second, divisible by 4) and timeval carry boundaries (1,000,000,000ns divisible by 1000) remain identical. The different intermediate low remainders are discarded by the unchanged divisions; finite rep_lo<4e9 keeps either addition below UINT32_MAX, and nsec+999 remains below signed 32-bit max. Infinite/narrowing branches are unchanged. Final POSIX seconds/fraction outputs are equivalent, including negative integral values and carry edges. No test-specific workaround observed. The double-modulo expression yields zero when the remainder is zero and divisor-remainder otherwise, matching the previously reviewed conditional formulation.

Every call to anonymous-namespace FloorToUnit passes a strictly positive finite unit (1ns,1us,1ms,1s,100ns). With these units, IDivDuration remainder has dividend sign, so q>0 implies nonnegative remainder; removing q>0 from the early-return predicate is redundant in this actual call graph. The MIN quotient underflow guard is retained, including negative infinity and saturated cases. ToUnixSeconds now uses FloorToUnit with 1s: for finite duration its high seconds field is mathematical floor, which the existing truncating quotient plus negative-remainder decrement reproduces; both infinities and finite MIN/MAX preserve saturated bounds. Internal hypothetical negative-unit calls are not claimed equivalent, and division has a different performance cost. No public value/API change or input-specific workaround observed.

The added !new_status.ok() skips assigning OK to an already-OK target. Pinned Status::ok() is exact equality to the canonical inline OK representation; when both objects are OK they have equal rep_. Both pinned copy and move assignment already do nothing when x.rep_ == old_rep, so the original does not consume the source in this both-OK case either. All error adoption, first-error preservation, payload sharing, and source move behavior are unchanged; self-update remains harmless. No test-specific workaround or observable value/ownership contract change found.

For a valid live StatusRep, the signed strong reference count starts at 1 and remains positive while any owning Status uses it. Under that representation invariant, <=1 and ==1 select exactly the same unique-owner fast path; shared refcounts >=2 still clone. Zero/dead objects, reference-count overflow/corruption, and concurrent mutation of the same Status are outside that invariant; this is not an all-bit-pattern equivalence claim. The acquire atomic ordering and shared-object cloning contract are preserved. No test-specific workaround observed.
